title: Introduce reservation safety-net and thresholdized burst controller for tenant burst isolation
creator: Liu Zhang
description:
Summary: After the 2026-02-12 dedicated cluster capacity incident we observed a multi-tenant eviction cascade where an initially noisy tenant with a highly spiky token-per-second pattern exhausted KV cache and GPU reservation headroom. This exposed two compounding issues: (1) several tenants had reservation levels that were systematically undersized relative to their actual burst distribution, and (2) the current burst policy allows instant 'full-burst' consumption which starved nearby tenants for critical scheduling slots.

Goal: Implement a pragmatic, low-risk mitigation that prevents single-tenant spike storms from causing cascading evictions while preserving low-latency bursts for healthy workloads. The proposal combines: a) a small ephemeral reservation safety-net that can be consumed only under strict backpressure conditions and automatically reconciled, and b) a thresholdized burst controller that enforces a burst consumption gradient rather than an all-or-nothing burst. This ticket tracks design, prototype, canary, and rollout for the safety-net + controller as part of the runtime-2.3.0 canary release.
postmortem_summary: Root cause: noisy tenant with sudden KV-cache churn and very short high-throughput bursts exposed under-provisioned reservation buckets and an overly permissive burst token logic. Contributing factors included lack of short-term emergency headroom and a burst allocator that did not respect per-tenant tail-latency budgets. Impact: elevated tail latency and a set of preemptive SDK evictions affecting ~8% of active Dedicated tenants for 27 minutes. Learned: need both proactive reservation sizing (forecast-driven) and reactive controls that limit instantaneous demand spikes in a graded manner.
action_items: Design and spec thresholdized burst controller (Aman) — deliver design doc and state machine by 2026-02-24: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Thresholdized-Burst-Controller
Implement ephemeral reservation safety-net (backend) (Priya Rao) — prototype branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5421 — target canary by 2026-03-05
Add predictive reservation estimator (offline model) (Data Eng) — expose hourly forecast API for reservation rebalancer by 2026-03-12
Integrate safety-net accounting and reconciliation (billing) (Finance-ops) — ensure we capture temporary credits and reconcile monthly by 2026-03-31
Create synthetic tenant workload tests and run in dedicated staging cluster (SRE) — create test harness and baseline reports by 2026-02-28
Run canary in two low-risk clusters for 48 hours, monitor eviction/latency dashboards, and collect telemetry (Aman + SRE) — canary window 2026-03-06 to 2026-03-08
Document rollback plan and emergency cutoff flags in Console (Product) — feature flag + kill-switch by 2026-03-04
tasks: Draft state machine and API surface for thresholdized burst controller
Prototype safety-net allocation and reconciliation hooks in allocator layer
Add metrics: safety-net-allocs, safety-net-reconciled, burst-gradient-used, tenant-burst-score
Create e2e synthetic workload runner that simulates noisy neighbor with KV churn
Implement server-side feature flag and runbook for quick disable
Update docs: runtime tuning guide and runbook section
acceptance_criteria: Canary shows >= 85% reduction in eviction correlation during synthetic noisy bursts compared to baseline
No increase in median latency for non-noisy tenants beyond 5% during canary
Safety-net allocations are reconciled within 15 minutes after burst ceases and appear in reconciliation logs
Feature flag can disable safety-net and controller with < 2s propagation time
Design doc reviewed and approved by runtime and SRE leads
comments: 2026-02-18 Liu Zhang: Created ticket after initial incident review. Proposed combined safety-net + threshold controller instead of hard tenant fencing to preserve PLG UX.
2026-02-20 Aman Patel: Posted initial state-machine draft. Key trade-off: safety-net size vs. frequency of reconciliation; recommended 5% ephemeral buffer per pool to start.
2026-02-22 Priya Rao: Prototype PR opened. Early tests show reduced eviction spikes but some increased scheduling jitter under maximum sustained bursts.
2026-02-24 SRE review (Anil Kumar): Requested additional telemetry for per-tenant KV cache pressure and suggested backpressure triggers include both queue depth and KV churn rate.

2026-02-28 QA: Synthetic harness completed; baseline run attached to ticket. Noted a regression in a rare path where safety-net reconciliation failed if a tenant resumed multi-minute bursts immediately after reconciliation — added fix to prototype.
2026-03-03 Product (Maya Lopez): Approved canary with the condition that a manual rollback target and kill-switch exist and that the Console exposes safety-net utilization to ops.
2026-03-05 Aman Patel: Canary scheduled for 2026-03-06. PR merged to canary branch with feature flag default-off. Metrics dashboards prepared and alert thresholds set.
resolution: Work in progress. Prototype merged to canary branch behind feature flag. Canary scheduled and will be validated against synthetic and live tenant signals. Planned full rollout if canary meets acceptance criteria and no customer-impacting regressions are found.
notes: This approach is intentionally conservative: ephemeral safety-net is small (configurable starting at 5% of pool) and reconciliation is strict to avoid billing surprises.
If the thresholdized gradient causes unexpected tail-latency increases, fallback is to reduce gradient aggressiveness and increase predictive reservation sizing until stable.
Follow-up ticket will track GA rollout, long-term predictive scaler integration, and policy UI in Console for tenant owners to opt-in/out.
